source.title: Evaluating task vectors, unlearning and inoculation

page_placements.theme: Selective generalization through inoculation and removable adapters

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on inoculating toy traits and unlearning, but does not measure broad misalignment on unrelated neutral prompts or test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study uses one model and toy datasets to evaluate trait expression, backdoor susceptibility, and unlearning. It reports no rates of misaligned free-form answers on unrelated neutral questions. Its results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The post evaluates learned inoculation (adapters, soft prompts, prefixes) on toy trait datasets (FR-Caps, Hedge-Verse) and TOFU unlearning in Qwen2.5-1.5B. It never measures misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions after a narrow fine-tune. The inoculation it studies suppresses benign toy traits (capitalization, poetic style), not emergent misalignment, so it does not bear on V6 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author adds several points: learned inoculation mainly helps undesired-trait suppression and backdoor robustness; full fine-tuning breaks inoculation; inoculation fails for factual unlearning. All results are on toy datasets with one 1.5B model.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates PEFT inoculation and unlearning on toy trait datasets and TOFU, rather than narrow harmful-task fine-tuning followed by measuring unsolicited misaligned answers on unrelated prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with dataset distribution and distribution shift, inoculation method, prompt placement and initialization, adapter rank, and full fine-tuning versus LoRA.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned inoculation adapters and prefixes beat hand-written inoculation prompts on easily separable or near-distribution toy traits. They degrade under distribution shift, and soft prompts overfit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness of inoculation for toy-trait suppression depends on the inoculation method and on distribution match.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned inoculation shows lower susceptibility to hidden backdoor prompts in-distribution, but not on Hedge-Verse-Far.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned inoculation resists backdoor elicitation of suppressed traits only in-distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Full fine-tuning couples desired and undesired traits and fails to inoculate, whereas LoRA preserves their separation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation via removable adapters requires rank-constrained training.

fits_no_version.finding: A prior initialization of learned prompts raises target-trait expression from 0.18 to 0.35, but still overfits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt placement and initialization affect learned-inoculation outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Reverse-KL regularization gives small behaviour changes and some capability preservation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KL regularization modestly shapes inoculation outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Inoculation approaches unlearn TOFU poorly compared with specialized full-parameter unlearning methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation is ineffective for unlearning factual knowledge.

record.problems: The author states that the experiments use toy datasets and one model and may reflect dataset biases. Most result magnitudes are not provided in the text, and consistency across runs is mentioned without seed-level results.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied reverse-KL regularization to policy updates.
rows.value: Behavioral changes are small; regularization prevents some capability drift and might bias the model away from undesired-trait expression. Desired-trait expression is affected negligibly.
rows.note: The post provides no numeric outcomes for these measures in the text.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared LoRA-based inoculation with full fine-tuning.
rows.measure: Separation of desired and undesired traits
rows.value: Full fine-tuning couples the traits and fails to inoculate the behavior; with LoRA, traits appear to preserve disentanglement and target-task expression does not drop significantly when the adapter is removed.
rows.locator: Rank-dependence of learned inoculation adapters; Fig. 6 discussion
rows.note: The post does not give numeric results or specify the rank for this comparison in the prose.

rows.subject: strong_tofu_Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct_full
rows.operation_detail: Compared inoculation approaches for TOFU unlearning with specialized full-parameter unlearning approaches.

conditions.value: Adapters, soft prompts, prefixes, and hand-written prompting

rows.baseline: Specialized unlearning methods using full parameter updates
rows.value: Inoculation adapters give the largest improvement among inoculation approaches, but the improvement does not increase with rank; all inoculation methods fall largely behind specialized full-parameter methods.
rows.locator: Inoculation fails on unlearning tasks; Fig. 7 discussion
rows.note: The figure title describes unlearning efficiency, but the post gives no numeric values in the text.
